title: channels__send — input
description: Input schema for the channels__send MCP tool. The tool is non-blocking: it returns as soon as the message is durably accepted by the backing store. Normative reference: spec/protocol.md and spec/ports/backing-store.md §2.1.

channel.description: Name of the target channel. Reserved prefixes enforce server-side access control: 'dm/<sorted-pair>' for direct messages (server-enforced two-party channels; only the two named agents may subscribe or send; wildcard subscription on this prefix is rejected); 'group/<group-id>' for managed group channels (server-enforced membership; only current members may subscribe or send; wildcard subscription on this prefix is rejected); 'sox/' for server-emitted derived channels (agents cannot write to sox/ channels). See docs/decisions/dm-semantics.md and docs/decisions/groups-model.md. Recommended conventions for open channels: 'ticket:<id>', 'broadcast:<topic>', 'thread:<parent-message-id>'.

body.description: Opaque message payload. MUST be a JSON object. SOX does not inspect or validate the body beyond requiring it to be an object. Recommended advisory fields: 'type' (string), 'subject' (string), 'context' (string), 'question' (string), 'answer' (string), 'urgency' (one of low/normal/high). Reserved body types with normative schemas: 'sox-error' (spec/envelopes/sox-error.schema.json), 'sox-invite' (spec/envelopes/sox-invite.schema.json).

correlation_id.description: Optional caller-supplied correlation token. Stored verbatim and echoed back in recv output. Use for: request-reply pairing, thread anchoring. The protocol does not enforce uniqueness. Null when not needed.

reply_to.description: Optional message_id of the message this message is replying to. Used for threading (combined with thread_depth on recv) and deadlock wait-graph computation. Null if this message is not a reply. See docs/decisions/threading-depth.md and docs/decisions/deadlock-detection-approach.md.

idempotency_key.description: Optional caller-supplied idempotency key. The server deduplicates sends with the same key within the configured TTL window (default 24 hours). A duplicate send returns the original message_id and sent_at without re-persisting. Callers MUST NOT rely on dedup beyond the TTL. Null disables idempotency for this send. See docs/decisions/idempotency-ttl.md.

body.subject: Which schema version to target?
body.context: Implementing the auth migration. The task spec mentions v2 but production shows v3.
body.question: Should I target schema v2 or v3?
